# `iscope_match_target_name`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Match the current view against the target catalogue and hold the result for iscope_accept_target_name.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds). Observer tier C |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xbdd80, MatchViewManualCaptureTarget @0x41cf80 (64-bit build); 32-bit success path also read |

No request parameters are read. In the local path the device lazily loads catalogue entries, computes a match from the goto or plate-solved centre and field of view, stores a pending-match ready flag and the original and matched names, and returns them. When the device is the master process in view mode 0 (with a wide-star-capable view) or modes 1 to 5, and it is not the selected master, the whole request is forwarded to the other process and that reply is returned instead; forwarded results and errors are unresolved. The cached match is written on both builds. Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0 replaces the old view-mode test with the relay-only form of the common relay check (it relays to the peer process when needed and runs no occupancy probe, so no 203 or 524 comes from it; READ in 64-bit firmware 9.75), the wire effect is INFERRED and the 32-bit build was not checked.

Side effects: Writes the pending-match ready flag and the original and matched names that later enable iscope_accept_target_name; may load catalogue entries into memory. Forwarded requests have a delegated wait of 10000 ms, which is not a whole-call deadline.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"iscope_match_target_name"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | Matching returned false: view mode is not 0 or the selected camera is not the main camera | `invalid request` |
| 300 | Forwarding helper has a null context | `internal error` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Relay and waiter failures on the forwarded path are propagated and not enumerated. Code 100 here comes from the handler, and shares its label with the dispatcher's invalid-request error.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":90,"method":"iscope_match_target_name"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"iscope_match_target_name","result":{"original_name":"Example target","matched_name":"Example target A","changed":true},"code":0,"id":90}
```

Reply, wrong-mode:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"iscope_match_target_name","error":"invalid request","code":100,"id":91}
```
